title: Slender-body L/B optimisation for minimum resistance at fixed displacement
objective_family: C_D and R_t versus length-to-diameter ratio, displacement volume held constant

geometry_family.why: closed-form wetted area and enclosed volume, so the fixed-displacement constraint can be applied exactly; the family passes through the published reference hull principal dimensions (L, D) where its wetted area is within 1.4 % of the published value, which is the geometry gate

datum.note: principal dimensions of the reference axisymmetric hull (see references.source); used only as the datum of the family, not as a claim that the offsets are identical

design.note: 3.0 m/s is the lowest published experimental condition of the reference hull, so the whole design sweep stays inside the resistance model's calibrated Froude envelope (Fr <= 0.62)

objectives.label: C_D = C_F + C_R (wetted-area basis, platform model)
R_t = 1/2 rho S V^2 C_D at fixed displacement [N]
R_t with Hoerner form factor (1+k) on the viscous term [N]
viscous + form drag only (wave term removed) [N]

form_factor.citation: Hoerner, S.F. (1965) Fluid-Dynamic Drag, ch. 6 (form factor of bodies of revolution)
form_factor.evidence_grade: literature correlation, applied at case level only (the platform solver has no form-factor term)

references.citation: Roddy, J.D. (1990) DARPA SUBOFF Model Experiments, DTRC-90/012 (as carried by the canonical platform dataset)
references.evidence_grade: REAL: experimental total-resistance coefficients with provenance in the canonical benchmark dataset

literature_anchors.statement: minimum-drag body of revolution at fixed volume, turbulent boundary layer: optimum fineness ratio about 4.5-5
literature_anchors.citation: Hoerner, S.F. (1965) Fluid-Dynamic Drag, ch. 6 (minimum-drag fineness-ratio discussion)
literature_anchors.evidence_grade: WITHHELD: quoted from the literature, not re-derived or independently verified offline; used as a consistency band only

literature_anchors.statement: underwater-vehicle design practice keeps L/D in about 7-8.5 (arrangement + structures + resistance trade-off)
literature_anchors.citation: design practice band, see note field
literature_anchors.note: this band is driven by arrangement/manoeuvring constraints as much as by drag; it is used as an order-of-magnitude consistency check, not as a measured drag optimum
literature_anchors.evidence_grade: WITHHELD: practice band, no single citable experiment
